'''Kimberly Kowal Arcand''' (born December 20, 1975) is a data visualizer and science communicator for [[NASA]]'s [[Chandra X-ray Observatory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Chandra X-ray Observatory |doi = 10.1036/1097-8542.801990|hdl = 2060/20010020257|hdl-access = free}}</ref> She is also the visualization coordinator for the [[Mathematical beauty|Aesthetics]] and Astronomy image response project at the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]]<ref>{{Citation |chapter=Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics |publisher=IOP Publishing Ltd |isbn=978-0333750889 |doi=10.1888/0333750888/4206 |title=The Encyclopedia of Astronomy and Astrophysics |year=2001 |citeseerx=10.1.1.248.447 }}</ref> located in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]].

== Early life and education==
As a child, Arcand wanted to be an [[astronaut]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://carnegiestemgirls.org/stem-resources/livin-it/kimberly-kowal-arcand/ |title=Kimberly Kowal Arcand - Carnegie STEM Girls |work=Carnegie STEM Girls |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-date=November 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191112164820/https://carnegiestemgirls.org/stem-resources/livin-it/kimberly-kowal-arcand/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> She studied [[molecular biology]] at the [[University of Rhode Island]] and also became a developer for the [[University of Rhode Island]] Center for Vector-Borne Disease Public Health project.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://tickencounter.org/about/our_team |title=TickEncounter Resource Center > About > Our Team |website=tickencounter.org |access-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180511050830/http://www.tickencounter.org/about/our_team |archive-date=May 11, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> She was awarded a fellowship with the [[Rhode Island]] Public Health Partnership to work on [[Lyme disease]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://chandra.harvard.edu/blog/node/294|title=Women in the High-Energy Universe: Kim Arcand {{!}} ChandraBlog {{!}} Fresh Chandra News|website=chandra.harvard.edu|access-date=November 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114141918/http://chandra.harvard.edu/blog/node/294|archive-date=November 14, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Arcand studied briefly at the  [[Harvard University]] Computer Science Department between 2000 and 2002.<ref name=":1" /> In 2013 Arcand earned a [[Master's degree]] in Public [[Humanities]] from [[Brown University]], focusing on image and meaning research.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Arcand |first1=Kimberly K. |last2=Watzke |first2=Megan |last3=Rector |first3=Travis |last4=Levay |first4=Zoltan G. |last5=DePasquale |first5=Joseph |last6=Smarr |first6=Olivia |date=August 8, 2013 |title=Processing Color in Astronomical Imagery |journal=Studies in Media and Communication |language=en |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=25–34 |doi=10.11114/smc.v1i2.198 |issn=2325-808X |arxiv=1308.5237 |bibcode=2013arXiv1308.5237A |s2cid=62543838 }}</ref> In 2020, Arcand completed her doctorate at the [[University of Otago]] in visualization science, under the supervision of [[Lisa F. Smith|Lisa Smith]].<ref name="pweb_Kimb">{{Cite web |title=Kimberly K. Arcand {{!}} Center for Astrophysics |author= |work=pweb.cfa.harvard.edu |date= |access-date=14 June 2021 |url=https://pweb.cfa.harvard.edu/people/kimberly-k-arcand |quote= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614195411/https://pweb.cfa.harvard.edu/people/kimberly-k-arcand |archive-date=14 June 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Arcand |first=Kimberly |year=2020 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Putting the stars within reach: NASA 3D data-based models in 3D print and virtual reality applications, and their potential effects on improving spatial reasoning skills and STEM interest in underrepresented groups of young female learners |publisher=OUR Archive, University of Otago |hdl=10523/10250 |url=https://ourarchive.otago.ac.nz/handle/10523/10250 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220523015225/https://ourarchive.otago.ac.nz/handle/10523/10250 |archive-date=2022-05-23 |access-date=2022-05-23 |url-status=live}}</ref> She worked in the [[University of Rhode Island]] Department of [[Computer science|Computer Science]] as an instructor between 1997 and 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fabfems.org/users/kimberly-arcand|title=Kimberly Arcand|website=fabfems.org|access-date=November 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181130071927/https://www.fabfems.org/users/kimberly-arcand|archive-date=November 30, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> She joined the [[Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory]] and [[Chandra X-ray Observatory]] in 1998.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.arcandwatzke.com/kim |title=Kimberly Arcand |website=Kimberly Arcand & Megan Watzke |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-date=March 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320063758/https://www.arcandwatzke.com/kim |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Career ==
[[file:Kimberly Arcand on vid in 2016.png|thumb|Arcand on ''[[This Week in Science]]'' in 2016 with Megan Watzke hosted by [[Kiki Sanford]]]]
[[File:Rendering Supernova Remnant Cassiopeia A into Virtual Reality.jpg|thumb|Arcand inside Brown University YURT, or VR CAVE, during testing of the headset and application.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://rocket-women.com/2017/12/meet-a-rocket-woman-kim-kowal-arcand-science-visualization-lead-for-nasa-chandra-x-ray-observatory-author/ |title=Meet A Rocket Woman: Kim Kowal Arcand, Science Visualization Lead, NASA's Chandra X-Ray Observatory & Author – Rocket Women |website=rocket-women.com |date=December 10, 2017 |access-date=December 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114141530/http://rocket-women.com/2017/12/meet-a-rocket-woman-kim-kowal-arcand-science-visualization-lead-for-nasa-chandra-x-ray-observatory-author/ |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>]]
[[File:SubjectMatterX Episode 005 Exploring the Universe with NASA's Kim Arcand, Visualization and Emerging Technology Lead for NASA's Flagship Chandra X-ray Observatory.ogg|thumb|Kim Arcand, Visualization and Emerging Technology Lead for NASA's Flagship Chandra X-ray Observatory, joins Todd Stewart and Bob Calise of Subjectmatterx.com to discuss the mysteries of the universe]]

In 2009 Arcand launched ''From Earth to the Universe'' with [[UNESCO]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fromearthtotheuniverse.org/event_photos.php |title=From Earth to the Universe Exhibition |website=www.fromearthtotheuniverse.org |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090129175149/http://www.fromearthtotheuniverse.org/event_photos.php |archive-date=January 29, 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref> She is the visualization coordinator of the Aesthetics and Astronomy image response project at the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://astroart.cfa.harvard.edu/about|title=About {{!}} Aesthetics & Astronomy|website=astroart.cfa.harvard.edu|access-date=November 14, 2018|archive-date=August 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822161624/http://astroart.cfa.harvard.edu/about|url-status=dead}}</ref> The project launched in 2010 and looks at variations in the presentation of color and scale in astronomical images. The team also studies how people respond to images, and the misconceptions that non-experts have when they view them.<ref name=":2" /> The project began when Randall, Jeffrey, and [[Lisa F. Smith]] realized that the art would provide astrophysicists a more effective way in conveying the results to a much larger audience.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2011/09/scientific-research-artfully-shown/ |title=Scientific research, artfully shown |date=September 22, 2011 |work=Harvard Gazette |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114182131/https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2011/09/scientific-research-artfully-shown/ |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The group explored the public perception of astronomical pictures using a survey linked to the [[NASA]] Astronomical Picture of the Day site.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Smith |first1=Lisa F. |last2=Smith |first2=Jeffrey K. |last3=Arcand |first3=Kimberly K. |last4=Smith |first4=Randall K. |last5=Bookbinder |first5=Jay |last6=Keach |first6=Kelly |date=August 18, 2010 |title=Aesthetics and Astronomy: Studying the Public's Perception and Understanding of Imagery From Space |journal=Science Communication |volume=33 |issue=2 |pages=201–238 |doi=10.1177/1075547010379579 |issn=1075-5470 |hdl=10523/6961|arxiv=1009.0772 |s2cid=118434018 }}</ref>

She worked closely with [[UNESCO]] to celebrate the [[International Year of Light]],<ref name=":3">{{Citation |last=Chandra X-ray Observatory |title=Light Beyond the Bulb: Bent Light in Space |date=October 13, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u-p4IakVWc8 |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190809195035/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u-p4IakVWc8 |archive-date=August 9, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> an open-source exhibition that showcased science based on light.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://lightexhibit.org/ |title=LIGHT: Beyond the Bulb |website=lightexhibit.org |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114114020/http://lightexhibit.org/ |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The celebration was supported by [[SPIE]].<ref name=":3" /> Using [[NASA]] data, Arcand developed a way to [[3D printing|3D print]] a supernova remnant.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chandra.si.edu/deadstar/deadstar.html |title=X-RAY UNIVERSE |website=chandra.si.edu |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303013606/http://chandra.si.edu/deadstar/deadstar.html |archive-date=March 3, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chandra.si.edu/vr/ |title=Walking among the stars |website=chandra.si.edu |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114182143/http://chandra.si.edu/vr/ |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Honors and awards ===
Arcand has won several awards for her work from [[NASA]] and the [[Smithsonian Institution]].

* 2007 [[Pirelli]] International Award for science communication<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://chandra.harvard.edu/press/07_releases/press_051707.html |title=Chandra Press Room :: Pirelli Award Recognizes Chandra Podcasts :: May 17, 2007 |website=chandra.harvard.edu |access-date=November 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119092045/http://chandra.harvard.edu/press/07_releases/press_051707.html |archive-date=November 19, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2010 [[International Year of Astronomy]] Mani Bhaumik Prize for Excellence in Astronomy Education and Public Outreach<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iau.org/news/pressreleases/detail/iau1002/|title=International Astronomical Union {{!}} IAU|website=www.iau.org|access-date=November 14, 2018|archive-date=November 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114223958/https://www.iau.org/news/pressreleases/detail/iau1002/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2014 Tech Collective ''Tech 10''<ref>{{Citation |last=TechCollectiveRI |title=Kimberly Kowal Arcand - 2014 Tech10 Award Winner |date=December 1, 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LOvQumkqi0I |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200327035735/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LOvQumkqi0I |archive-date=March 27, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref>
* 2016 [[Smithsonian Institution]] Achievement Award<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://smithsonianeducation.org/educationawards_recipients.html |title=Past Smithsonian Education Award Recipients |website=smithsonianeducation.org |access-date=November 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181119091911/http://smithsonianeducation.org/educationawards_recipients.html |archive-date=November 19, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Publications ==
=== Authored and co-authored ===

Arcand has written several popular science books. Her book ''Colouring the Universe'' was selected by Cosmos as one of the Top Illustrated Science Books of 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cosmosmagazine.com/space/the-top-illustrated-science-books-of-2016|title=Top illustrated science books of 2016 {{!}} Cosmos|website=cosmosmagazine.com|access-date=November 14, 2018|archive-date=April 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422003855/https://cosmosmagazine.com/space/the-top-illustrated-science-books-of-2016/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She collaborates with [[Megan Watzke]] and [[Travis Rector]], Ph.D.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.scientia.global/kimberly-kowal-arcand-science-diffusion/ |title=Kimberly Kowal Arcand - Somewhere, Outside The Rainbow • scientia.global |date=February 23, 2017 |work=scientia.global |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114210753/https://www.scientia.global/kimberly-kowal-arcand-science-diffusion/ |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Her book ''Light: The Visible Spectrum and Beyond'' was selected by [[Forbes]] as one of the Top 10 Gifts of 2016.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/startswithabang/2016/12/08/top-10-gifts-for-lovers-of-outer-space/#3e4d246d7a5e |title=Top 10 Gifts For Lovers Of Outer Space |last=Siegel |first=Ethan |work=Forbes |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114182609/https://www.forbes.com/sites/startswithabang/2016/12/08/top-10-gifts-for-lovers-of-outer-space/#3e4d246d7a5e |archive-date=November 14, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>
